# pve_ceph_mon (Resource)

Creates and destroys one Ceph monitor on a node (`POST/DELETE /nodes/{node}/ceph/mon/{monid}`). PVE auto-creates a Manager for the first monitor. All attributes force replacement because the pin defines no monitor update verb.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pve_ceph_mon" "pve1" {
  node        = "pve1"
  mon_address = "10.0.0.11"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `node` (String) Name of the PVE node the monitor is created on; PVE defaults the monitor id to this node name.

### Optional

- `mon_address` (String) Overwrites the autodetected monitor IP address(es); must be in the public network(s) of Ceph (pin `mon-address`).
- `monid` (String) The ID for the monitor (pattern: alphanumeric with inner alphanumerics or dashes, max 200). When omitted, PVE defaults it to the node name, which the provider resolves into state after create.

### Read-Only

- `addr` (String) Ceph-formatted monitor address as advertised by the monitor (typically `IP:PORT/NONCE`, possibly a messenger-v2 vector).
- `ceph_version` (String) Full Ceph version string of the monitor daemon.
- `host` (String) Host the monitor runs on.
- `in_quorum` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is part of the current quorum.
- `rank` (Number) Rank of the monitor within the mon map.
- `service` (Boolean) Whether a `ceph-mon@<id>` systemd unit is enabled on the hosting node.
- `state` (String) Run state of the monitor: `running` (in quorum), `stopped` (systemd unit configured but daemon not visible to the cluster), or `unknown` (no rados access).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing monitor by its node and monitor id:
terraform import pve_ceph_mon.pve1 pve1:pve1
```
